commit_message:
riscv: Provide a vector only implementation of Chacha20 cipher

Although we have a Zvkb version of Chacha20, the Zvkb from the RISC-V
Vector Cryptography Bit-manipulation extension was ratified in late 2023
and does not come to the RVA23 Profile. Many CPUs in 2024 currently do not
support Zvkb but may have Vector and Bit-manipulation, which are already in
the RVA22 Profile. This commit provides a vector-only implementation that
replaced the vror with vsll+vsrl+vor and can provide enough speed for
Chacha20 for new CPUs this year.

Signed-off-by: Yangyu Chen <cyy@cyyself.name>

Reviewed-by: Paul Dale <ppzgs1@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/24069)

fix_commit_message:
Fix riscv64 chacha crash due to unaligned data

The linux-riscv64 test machine crashes due to unaligned data,
when the V extension is enabled, while QEMU seems to have no
problems with unaligned data.

So check for aligned data and fall back to C code in case the
input or output values are unaligned.

Reviewed-by: Paul Dale <ppzgs1@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/28684)
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 22417bc14d6b on top of intro 03ce37e11729 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (LogicError): On riscv64, OpenSSL's ChaCha20_ctr32() dispatcher chooses a vectorized (RVV/Zbb/Zvkb) assembly implementation of ChaCha20 whenever the CPU advertises the relevant extensions and the input length exceeds one block, without verifying that the input and output buffer pointers are properly aligned. The vector assembly routines perform vector loads/stores that assume aligned memory; on real riscv64 hardware with the V extension enabled, unaligned `out`/`inp` pointers cause a crash (bus error / illegal instruction), even though the same code runs fine under QEMU emulation which is more permissive about misaligned vector accesses. Root cause: The feature-detection-based dispatch logic for selecting the RISC-V vector ChaCha20 implementation checked only CPU capability flags (RISCV_HAS_ZBB, riscv_vlen, RISCV_HAS_ZVKB) and input length, but never validated pointer alignment of the `out`/`inp` buffers before invoking vector load/store based assembly routines that require (or strongly prefer) aligned accesses on real hardware.
